content: A brownout, also referred to as a grey-out, is a temporary loss of vision that is characterized by a dimming of light, often accompanied by a brownish tint and a reduction in peripheral vision. This phenomenon is typically a warning sign of an impending fainting episode or blackout. It is frequently observed when an individual stands up abruptly, particularly in cases of orthostatic hypotension. Recovery from a brownout is usually quick, and the condition can often be reversed by lying down. In some cases, a brownout can be intentionally induced, though this is strongly discouraged. For example, hyperventilation, which is discussed in the context of the choking game under self-induced hypocapnia, can lead to a brownout. Hyperventilation may also unintentionally cause a brownout, as seen in shallow water blackout scenarios. Additionally, brownouts are commonly experienced by aircraft pilots who are subjected to high positive G-forces, such as during a sharp pull-up into a loop or a tight turn. This is the opposite of a redout, which involves a reddening of vision due to negative G-forces, such as those experienced during an outside loop when the aircraft's nose is pushed downward. Redouts are particularly hazardous as they can result in retinal damage and hemorrhagic stroke. To mitigate the effects of brownouts, pilots of high-performance aircraft often wear G-suits. These suits help prevent blood from pooling in the lower limbs, thereby maintaining adequate blood flow to the brain. However, no suit currently exists to counteract the effects of a redout. Prolonged or intense G-forces, if not addressed, can lead to G-force-induced Loss of Consciousness (G-LOC). Brownouts are also a common occurrence among roller coaster riders. Many roller coasters subject riders to high positive G-forces, particularly during vertical loops and helices. However, roller coasters rarely generate sufficient negative G-forces to cause redouts, as low-G elements are typically designed to simulate a sensation of weightlessness rather than exerting extreme forces. Another situation in which a grey-out may occur is after donating blood. However, the onset of such grey-outs is usually gradual and can often be prevented by lying down, which allows blood to flow to the brain more easily without having to work against gravity.
